12.16.s.en: 12. The tongue of the wise and the tongue of fools!

12.16.0.en: 17 He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit. 18 There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health. 19 The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment. 20 Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace is joy. 21 There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief. 22 Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight.

12.16.1.en: In the following verses [17-22] the wise man speaks of the tongue of the wise and, in contrast to it, the lying tongue of the wicked. The wise speak the truth and do not know lying; this is the delight of God Himself, for He is the Truth who knows no falsehood. The wicked, however, find lying sweet and rejoice in it, and it is an abomination to the Lord, who cannot bear falsehood, lying, deceit or malice.

12.16.2.en: "He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit." [17]

12.16.3.en: The tongue often reveals what is in the heart. He who speaks the truth bears witness to the righteousness or justice that is established in his heart. But he who speaks falsehood reveals the crookedness and deceit that are in his heart.

12.16.4.en: * "Abba Pishoy the deacon said: I once said to our two Roman fathers (Maximus and Domadius): 'If you were in Constantinople now, we would surely find you two to be kings now.' They turned their faces toward me and said to me gently: 'Where is your spirit, brother, that you said this word? We have told you several times, brother Pishoy, that whether you are sitting with us or in your dwelling, you must always hold fast, without ceasing, to the saving name of our Lord Jesus Christ, for in truth, if this most holy name were in your heart, you would not have said this word that you have just uttered. For if we neglect this most holy name, we shall surely die in our sins. Let us hate freedom (in speech), joking and vain words, which scatter all the fruit of the monk. When we were in Syria, people tried to make us happy without letting us think about our sins; but exile and silence, with understanding and the endurance of hardships, these are the characteristics of our race. For hardship begets prayer in purity, and prayer begets the fear of God and love, and this is what makes the man; for surely neither rank nor wealth nor courage is honored before God, but the holy soul that seeks Him and His sacrifice and offering; this is our salvation."

12.16.5.en: The Paradise of the Fathers * Do not allow the spirit of lying to be found in you, lest the Lord deliver you to destruction.

12.17.0.en: St. Abba Paula of Tamouh "There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health." [18]

12.17.1.en: He who pours out wounding or even gentle words, under the guise of joking and merriment, is pouring out poisons, and is like one who stabs others with a sword, as he stabs himself. But earnest words that have the touch of the quiet Spirit heal wounds and support others, and also build up his own soul.

12.17.2.en: * Familiarity, joking and laughter are like a fire that is kindled in a reed and destroys.

12.17.3.en: Abba Agathon * Because we do not guard ourselves against small slips, we fall into great ones. For example, a man's laughing at a time when it is not the time for laughter draws another into laughter, and then he says: What harm is there in laughing? Then the fear of God begins to be uprooted from him; then from laughter comes joking, and from joking foul speech, and from this come blameworthy deeds. Thus the deceiving enemy makes small slips easy for us, and from them draws us into great sins, and from there leads us to despair. By this gradual progress he draws us into matters in a hidden manner. We must therefore drive away his thoughts from their very beginning, and not be careless about small things, for the enemy lies in wait in them to drag us into great ones. For if he fought us openly, his fighting would be easy for us and his defeat within our reach; but he sets for us ambushes and snares from which we cannot quickly free ourselves.

12.18.0.en: St. John Chrysostom "The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment." [19]

12.18.1.en: He who speaks the truth abides in God, the Truth, and his words become immortal, accompanying him to eternity as a secret of his glory. But the lying tongue clings to the devil, the liar and father of liars, and in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, its lie and deceit are exposed, and its plans are destroyed as its life is destroyed.

12.19.0.en: "Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace is joy." [20]

12.19.1.en: What a man utters returns to him and works upon his depths more than its effect on others. He who speaks evil reaps in his heart and mind deceit and evil, and he who offers counsel of peace enjoys inner joy in his depths.

12.20.0.en: There shall no evil happen to the just: but the wicked shall be filled with mischief." [21]

12.20.1.en: The wicked exert every effort to trouble the righteous and to inflict harm on him, but their evils return upon them and do the righteous no harm. And the righteous exerts every effort to do good to others, and the first to benefit from these good things is the righteous himself.

12.21.0.en: "Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight." [22]

12.21.1.en: Every word we utter, whether for the benefit and good of others or for their harm, God reckons as directed to Himself personally. So He delights in those who speak the truth, and cannot bear lying and deceit.

12.22.s.en: 13. Quietness with knowledge, not ignorance with chatter

12.22.0.en: "A prudent man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness." [v. 23]

12.22.1.en: The wise man, even if he speaks few words, hides behind them true and honored knowledge; but the fool cries out at the top of his voice, and in chatter reveals the ignorance and folly in his heart. He exposes himself by the multitude of his words.

12.23.0.en: "The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the slothful shall be under tribute." [24]

12.23.1.en: Many have gifts and abilities, but because they are slack and lazy they gain nothing from their gifts; rather these become a judgment against them, and through their laziness they come into humiliation, like those who are under tribute. For our life on earth is a time for earnest work.

12.23.2.en: Perhaps the most important of the sins that seem trivial but are destructive is carelessness or laziness, and as St. Cyril the Great says: [Since Paul knows that laziness is the door of destruction, he says: "Woe is unto me, if I preach not" (1 Cor 9:16).]

12.23.3.en: Let us be sober and watchful, lest our portion be with that woman whom Hermas saw, when he saw the sluggish soul as an old woman, worn out and reclining on a chair, unable to move. When he asked the reason, he was told: [Because your spirit is now an old woman who has lost her strength by reason of your weaknesses and doubts. She has become like old men who have lost hope of renewing their strength, and no longer expect anything except that they will sink into their last sleep. So you have become weak through worldly preoccupations, and have handed your souls over to sluggishness, and have not cast your care upon God (1 Pet 5:7).

12.23.4.en: * "Wilt thou be made whole?" (Jn 5:6)... The Lord asked (the sick man at Bethesda), not in order to know (whether he wished to be healed), for He had no need of that, but He wanted to show forth the man's perseverance, and that because of it he had left the others and come to Him...

12.23.5.en: The perseverance of the paralytic is astonishing: for thirty-eight years he had been hoping every year to be healed of his sickness. He continued lying there and did not withdraw from the pool...

12.23.6.en: Let us be ashamed, beloved, let us be ashamed and sigh over the greatness of our slackness.

12.23.7.en: For thirty-eight years he waited without obtaining what he longed for, and yet he did not withdraw. He did not fail through any neglect on his part, but through the pressure of others, their violence and their troubles. All this did not make him dull. Whereas we, if we persevere in prayer for ten days for some matter and do not obtain it, our zeal grows slack.

12.24.0.en: "Heaviness in the heart of man maketh it stoop: but a good word maketh it glad." [25]

12.24.1.en: St. Anthony says that just as the body needs its food to sustain and refresh it, so the soul needs joy. But gloom, anxiety and agitation bow the soul down and shatter it.

12.24.2.en: It is fitting for the believer to rejoice and to make the hearts of others glad with a good word, as the Apostle Paul says: "Comfort the feebleminded" (1 Thess 5:14). And Job says: "How forcible are right words!" (Job 6:25).

12.25.s.en: 16. The two paths of righteousness and evil

12.25.0.en: The righteous guides his companion, but the way of the wicked leads them astray. 27 Slackness catches no game, but the precious wealth of man is diligence. 28 In the way of righteousness is life; and in the pathway thereof there is no death.

12.25.1.en: "The righteous guides his companion, but the way of the wicked leads them astray." [26]

12.25.2.en: He who is sincere and pure in heart supports himself as he builds up his brother; but the wicked man tears down his own life and strays from the true way.

12.26.0.en: "Slackness catches no game, but the precious wealth of man is diligence." [27]

12.26.1.en: He who walks the way of righteousness lives faithful and diligent, while he who walks the way of evil lives slack. The first carries a treasure in his heart, for he is faithful in little, diligent and earnest in his life, and goes from success to success. But the second is lazy, and whatever his possibilities and abilities, he only hunts the wind.

12.26.2.en: Ruth gleaned the fallen ears all day long until evening (Ruth 2:17), so her story was recorded in the Holy Bible, and she was made worthy to bear Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David the prophet, from whose seed the Lord Christ came incarnate!

12.26.3.en: The lazy servant who buried his talent in the earth became worthy of eternal punishment (Mt 25:14-30).

12.27.0.en: "In the way of righteousness is life; and in the pathway thereof there is no death." [28]

12.27.1.en: The way of righteousness or love shines day by day until the day of the Lord comes, and those who walk in it are made worthy of eternal life. Their bodily death is turned into a passing over to eternity. They sing, saying: "For this God is our God for ever and ever: he will be our guide even unto death" (Ps 48:14).

12.27.2.en: Truly blessed is the believer who passes through the way of righteousness in the midst of this wicked world, and goes forth with love for all to the city of God, the heavenly Jerusalem.

12.27.3.en: * That we may not be among the murderers or among the living dead, let us strive to love, not only our friends, but our enemies also. By this we can meet the merciful and compassionate Lord with a simple conscience in keeping with the bond of His pledge.

12.27.4.en: * The ways of the wicked who think of harm are death (Prov 12:28). "Thou shalt not think harm against thy brother" (Lev 19:18) LXX. And also: [If you see the donkey of one who hates you fallen (in the mire), do not pass by it unless you first lift it up] (cf. Ex 23:5). Everyone must keep in mind that it is not permitted to leave the donkey of his enemy in the mire; how then can a man hate or ignore one created in the image of God? I have noticed in the blessed Job a sincere and perfect love in all faithfulness, even toward his enemies, so that he was able to rejoice and to say to the Lord with a clear conscience: "If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him, and said in my heart: Well!" (Job 31:29).

12.27.5.en: * By loving a man who is your enemy you become a friend of God; in truth not only His friend but also His son, as the Lord Himself says: [Love your enemies, do good to them that hate you; this proves that you are the sons of your Father in heaven] (cf. Mt 5:44-45)... Let us strive to act as physicians toward all the wicked. Let us hate their evil deeds, not the people themselves. Let us pray for all the good, that they may always rise to a better life, and for the wicked, that they may quickly enjoy a good life through the medicines of repentance. When we pray for this, He grants it to us also.

12.27.6.en: * (Stephen) grieved more over their sins than over his wounds. He grieved over their evils more than over his death. He acted rightly; surely there was in their evil conduct what required mourning, while there was nothing in his death to grieve over. Eternal death followed their evil, while life without end followed his death... Would that we loved our brethren in the Church with the same spirit with which Stephen loved his enemies.

12.27.7.en: Fr. Caesarius, Bishop of Arles * Why should we spend more time in citing the apostolic and evangelical commandments, when the old Law, which is thought to be somewhat lenient, warns against the same thing, when it says: "Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart," and also: "Thou shalt not be wroth against the children of thy people" (Lev 19:17-18). So also it says: [The ways of those who are wroth lead to death] (cf. Prov 12:28). Thus you see that evil is forbidden, not in deed only, but also in the hidden recesses of thought, according to the commandment that calls for the uprooting of evil from the heart, not merely taking vengeance for the wrong done to us, but even thinking about it.

12.27.9.en: Sanctify me, that I may pass over to You

12.27.10.en: * Who can lead me to You?

12.27.11.en: Your grace is the guide of my life.

12.27.12.en: May it extend and work in me with tenderness as with discipline.

12.27.13.en: * Your Holy Spirit works in my heart as in my mind.

12.27.14.en: He grants me goodness, so that my depths are filled with love of good for all.

12.27.16.en: And evil finds no place in me.

12.27.17.en: * Let me be united with You, and love Your commandment and Your word.

12.27.18.en: Then my depths will be built upon the rock of Your teachings.

12.27.19.en: The whirlwinds of the worlds cannot shake me.

12.27.20.en: The foundations of my soul are not shaken, for they are built upon You, O Rock of ages!

12.27.21.en: * Your Spirit beautifies my soul and renews it, making of it a beautiful bride, adorned with the fruit of the Spirit.

12.27.22.en: He makes of it a crowned queen, honored by the heavenly ones.

12.27.23.en: * Your Spirit sanctifies my thoughts, my words and my deeds, that I may bear witness to Your righteousness and enjoy Your salvation.

12.27.24.en: He builds a holy temple that death does not destroy, nor time corrupt, but which increases in splendor and glory day by day.

12.27.25.en: * I have nothing to seek but the divine wisdom.

12.27.26.en: So I ask You uprightly, that I may pass over to You.

12.27.27.en: I ask nothing of the world, for You satisfy my whole being!

12.27.28.en: * Grant me Your love, that I may be tender even toward the dumb animals; even in my contention, let nothing proceed from me but tenderness.

12.27.29.en: Let violence have no authority over my depths.

12.27.30.en: Grant me the contention of the gentle dove, not the kisses of the deceiving, ravening wolves.

12.27.31.en: * My soul groans with love for the sinners.

12.27.32.en: They set nets for me, and fell into them.

12.27.33.en: They wanted to snare me, and became the prey of their own evils.

12.27.34.en: Their plots were turned into a crown of glory for my weakness.

12.27.35.en: The cup they filled for me, they drank.

12.27.36.en: And what they sowed, they reaped.
